source: SHA256-verified original 256 source rows in audit_resource_pollen_shapley.json, reproduced from original 2026-10-06 t400 evolving diploid checkpoint
question: At what prespecified resource-scale levels is the original K48 census ceiling no longer hiding a seed-output contrast, and does the group loss or gain sign persist across history clusters?
theory: At fixed original genotypes/visitors/assurance/investment, scaling ovule_budget by factor b scales source maternal viable seed expectation linearly; pollen transfer/delivery unchanged. With no adults surviving and no immigrant seeds, one-step N' = min(Poisson(b*mu), K48), P(N'>0)=1-exp(-b*mu). Compute analytic means and probabilities without drawing new random populations.
admission_rule: No parameter chosen or retuned from outcomes; report ALL six budgets and all four reproductive settings with original 64 historical pairs. This is an old-data exploratory diagnostic, not prospectively independent confirmation.
primary_descriptives: mean source per-history E-minus-I-clamp expected next census at each b
mean occupancy probability difference at each b
mean native source viable maternal seed contrast scaled by b
cluster_eligibility: All 64 original histories retained, one of original eight demographic repeats, no new independent history
uncertainty: One shared 9999-draw history bootstrap seed 20261010, unadjusted descriptive intervals across all four settings/six scales, not inferential promotion
null_expectations: At b=1, source next census effects should be almost 0 owing to K48 saturation
At b very small, E-minus-clamp census contrast approaches scaled viable maternal seed contrast, but one-step occupancy may remain saturated or floor depending b
If source seed contrast is mixed, census effect will also be mixed, not universal
decision_gate: If no budget provides intermediate one-step occupancy and consistent positive/negative grouped census contrasts at history level, STOP. Do not use post-outcome chosen single budget to launch repeated 80-update stochastic histories.
